email.subject: New sign-in to your TeamChat account

body.v: We detected a sign-in to your TeamChat account from a new device in another country. If it wasn't you, please secure your account within the next few hours.
Thank you for helping us keep TeamChat safe.

hotspots.explain: teamchat-support.example is not teamchat.example, TeamChat's domain. Anyone can buy a domain name that looks official.
A foreign country and "within the next few hours": enough to worry you into clicking without thinking.
The button leads to teamchat-secure.example, yet another domain that isn't the real one.
A signature takes two seconds to copy. It proves nothing either way.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone imitating TeamChat. The display name looks right, but the address is on teamchat-support.example instead of teamchat.example.
choices: Someone with an address imitating TeamChat

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Fear, then hurry: a stranger may be in your account, and you only have a few hours.
choices: Fear of a break-in, with a tight deadline

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Click the button and sign in. Your login details would go straight to the sender.
choices: Click the button and sign in

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Don't use the button. Open the TeamChat app yourself and look at the list of signed-in devices.
choices: Click the link to find out for sure
Reply and ask whether the alert is real
Open the app yourself and check your devices

actions.label: Open the TeamChat app yourself and check your devices
actions.consequence: Only your own devices are listed. The alert was made up.

actions.label: Click "Secure my account" and sign in
actions.consequence: The page looks every bit like TeamChat, but your login details go straight to the scammer.

actions.label: Reply and ask whether the alert is genuine
actions.consequence: The scammer confirms it, naturally, and pushes harder. Along the way, you've proved your address is active.

actions.label: Report it as phishing, then delete it
actions.consequence: Nothing was clicked, and the message is no longer sitting in your inbox.

attacker_reveal: A sign-in that never happened, a faraway country, a few hours to react: fear did half the work. As for the address, you had to read it letter by letter to see what was wrong.
